text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on September 24 in history.
1834 - King Pedro IV of Portugal died and was succeeded by Queen Maria II. Better known as Dom Pedro, he also founded the Brazilian Empire and ruled it from 1822-31.
1852 - Henri Giffard, a French engineer, made the first powered flight in a dirigible. The steam-powered airship travelled 17 miles (27 km) from Paris to Trappes.

1869 - Jay Gould and James Fisk tried to corner the gold bullion market in the United States. The government responded by releasing gold on to the market, causing panic and a slump in its price. The event became known as "Black Friday".
1884 - Ismet Inonu, Turkish general and statesman, born. President from 1938-50, he succeeded Mustafa Kemal (Ataturk).
1911 - Konstantin Chernenko, Soviet politician, born. He took over as Soviet president from Yuri Andropov in February 1984 and was succeeded by Mikhail Gorbachev on his death in 1985.

1941 - Nine allied governments meeting in London pledged allegiance to the Atlantic Charter, an eight-point declaration issued during World War Two by U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill.
1957 - U.S. President Dwight Eisenhower ordered the National Guard to enforce racial integration of schools in Little Rock, Arkansas.
1960 - The first U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, the USS Enterprise, was launched from Newport, Virginia.
1965 - The constitutional conference on Mauritius ended in London, deciding that the country should become an independent state within the Commonwealth by the end of 1966.
1971 - Ninety Russian diplomats were expelled from Britain for spying following revelations made by a Soviet defector.
1972 - In a referendum, Norwegians voted 53.5 percent to 46.5 percent against joining the European Economic Community.
1975 - Britons Dougal Haston and Doug Scott became the first to climb Mount Everest by the south-west face.
1980 - A simmering border war between Iran and Iraq flared into full-scale hostilities when Iraqi troops crossed the border and encircled Abadan, setting fire to the world's biggest oil refinery.
1983 - Dame Isobel Baillie, Scottish soprano who gave over 1,000 performances of Handel's "Messiah", died.

1983 - Five business executives received jail sentences of up to five years for their role in the 1976 environmental disaster in Seveso, Italy, when a cloud of dioxin gas was released after an explosion.
1988 - At the Olympic Games in Seoul, Canadian Ben Johnson set a new world record of 9.79 seconds for the 100 metres. Six days later he was stripped of his medal for taking drugs.
1990 - West German President Richard von Weizsaecker signed a 1,000-page treaty making the October 3 reunification of the two Germanys official.

1990 - East Germany, once Moscow's chief frontline ally, left the Warsaw Pact ahead of unification with NATO member West Germany. East Germany had joined the Pact with seven other Communist states when the Soviet-dominated group was founded in 1955.

1993 - Norodom Sihanouk reclaimed the Cambodian throne he gave up in 1955. He also signed into law a new constitution officially proclaiming his ravaged country a democratic and constitutional monarchy.

1993 - Former Philippine first lady Imelda Marcos, whose extravagance helped bring down her husband's government, was convicted of corruption and sentenced to at least 18 years in jail. She remains free on bail while the Supreme Court considers her appeal.
1995 - Somali warlord Mohamed Farah Aideed's self-proclaimed government said Libya had become the first country to recognise it.
